newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Thursday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.03/1.98 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 2.10/2.05 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.93/1.88 percent against 2.10/2.05 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.45/99.50 from Wednesday's close of S$99.38/99.48, September 2001 was unchanged from Wednesday's close of S$96.60/96.70 and June 2003 ended at S$94.70/94.75 versus S$94.60/94.65.
The interbank rate was unchanged from Wednesday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
